problem_statement: RuchiraSachinthana/Portfolio-Website is a static single-page developer portfolio built on the iPortfolio (Bootstrap) template, served directly from static files, with a left icon-nav rail and stacked sections (About, Facts, Skills, Resume, Portfolio, Services, Testimonials, Contact) plus a separate portfolio-details page. Upgrade the Portfolio section's category filter into a genre-native Filter works control: a chip row above the works grid with category chips (All, Web Design, Graphic Design, Photography) and a live result readout 'Showing N of 9 . <Category>' over the grid of 9 work cards. Clicking a category chip must filter the works grid to that category AND recompute the readout (e.g. 'Showing 3 of 9 . Graphic Design'). The Filter works chip strip also appears as a compact teaser in the About and Contact sections so category browsing stays continuous down the page. The chip row must be responsive (wrap on a 390px phone with no horizontal overflow) and the works grid must render as a tidy multi-column grid with legible card titles and readable active-chip contrast. Keep the template's light theme, blue (#149ddd) accent, and icon-nav rail intact.
required_content: The Portfolio section shows a 'Filter works' chip row with four category chips and a live 'Showing N of 9 . <Category>' readout above a grid of 9 work cards.
Clicking a category chip filters the works grid AND updates the readout; clicking Graphic Design yields 'Showing 3 of 9 . Graphic Design'.
The Filter works chip strip appears as a compact teaser in the About and Contact sections (cross-section continuity).
At 390px the chip row wraps and the page has no horizontal overflow; the works grid stays a tidy legible multi-column grid on desktop with readable active-chip contrast.
Each work card shows its title, category, and thumbnail.
No new JavaScript console errors or failed network requests (beyond the template's pre-existing third-party font/chat-widget hosts) are introduced.
design_constraints: Preserve the iPortfolio light theme, blue (#149ddd) accent, and left icon-nav rail.
The Filter works chip row must ride above the works grid it controls (Portfolio section) and as a compact teaser in About + Contact; do not make it a separate page or hero banner.
The category chip row must be responsive (wrap / flexible chips), not a fixed-width nowrap row that overflows the mobile viewport.
The works grid must be a tidy multi-column grid; cards must not shingle or overlap via negative margins, and card titles / active-chip text must stay legible (no near-white-on-white).
Clicking a chip must recompute the readout from the active category; a frozen/stale readout that never updates is a defect.
Only the Filter-works markup/stylesheet/script and its teaser presence change between legs; the shared theme, sections, and nav rail stay the same.
state_constraints: desktop_portfolio captures the Portfolio section at 1440px: the Filter works chip row renders four category chips in one tidy responsive row above a legible multi-column works grid, active chip readable, readout 'Showing 9 of 9 . All'.

mobile_portfolio captures the same section at 390px: the responsive chip row wraps and the page has no horizontal overflow (a fixed-width nowrap chip row would push the document wider than the viewport).
desktop_about and desktop_contact show the compact Filter works teaser (cross-section continuity); desktop_details captures the portfolio-details page (shared theme regression surface).
desktop_portfolio_graphic captures the Portfolio section after clicking the Graphic Design chip: the grid filters to 3 works and the readout recomputes to 'Showing 3 of 9 . Graphic Design'.
Source inspection confirms a static iPortfolio template; the Filter works lever lives inline in index.html, its layout in assets/css/pf.css, and its behavior in assets/js/pf.js.

change_completion: The Portfolio section shows the Filter works chip row with four category chips and a live 'Showing N of 9 . <Category>' readout above a 9-work grid.
Clicking the Graphic Design chip filters the grid to 3 works and updates the readout to 'Showing 3 of 9 . Graphic Design'.
The Filter works teaser appears in the About and Contact sections.
design_consistency: The chip row keeps the template's light theme, blue accent, and icon-nav rail.
The works grid is a tidy multi-column grid with legible card titles and readable active-chip contrast (no overlap, no white-on-white).
Desktop and tablet appearance of the chip row and grid are preserved.
regression: The section navigation, icon-nav rail, work lightbox links, and portfolio-details page remain functional.
No new console errors or failed network requests (beyond the template's pre-existing third-party font/chat-widget hosts) are introduced.
responsive: At 390px the chip row wraps and the page has no horizontal overflow or clipped chips.
The works grid collapses cleanly on mobile without overlapping cards.

author_notes: Repo-grounded static iPortfolio developer portfolio (RuchiraSachinthana/Portfolio-Website; source zip confirmed by exact SHA 4304df2e4897). capability=Upgrade the Portfolio section's own category filter into a genre-native Filter works lever: category chips + a live 'Showing N of 9' readout + a filtered works grid, plus a compact teaser in About and Contact. The three legs vary only in the Filter-works markup in index.html, assets/css/pf.css (chip-row responsiveness + works-grid layout), assets/js/pf.js (filter wiring), and the per-section presence of the compact teaser. The shared theme, sections, nav rail, and portfolio imagery are declared infrastructure, identical across all three legs. As infrastructure (all legs): the template's self-contained Isotope filter is disabled so the new pf.js owns the filter, AOS scroll-reveal is disabled so content is static-visible, the remote Jivochat widget is removed, and the `section { overflow: hidden }` clamp is relaxed so horizontal overflow is observable at the document level (reference wraps -> 0px). Served directly as static files; reference is runtime-clean (0 new console errors, 0 failed same-origin requests).
